steps.text: Hiss—
Huff—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hiss—

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You can take off the breather, Magallan. There are no spores here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, okay.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whew... hah...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I've never been so scared of mushrooms in my life.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I warned you, Maggy: Don't touch anything, don't touch anything, and don't touch anything.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Now you know why.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: M-My—

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The empty box you gave me? I put the mushrooms inside and sealed it. Here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Th-Thanks.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: *pant*—*pant*—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I didn't expect the spore density to be so high, or that it could paralyze the respiratory system.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's a carnivorous mushroom. Where do you think its food comes from?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So how come you aren't affected at all?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: We hunters have ways to deal with them.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: If I died in one of those mushroom swamps, I'd never live it down.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Sami) Typhon, the sacrifice.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (Sami) Sacrifice... are we there?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Where are you going? Wait for me!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And what do you by 'sacrifice'? Me?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Of course not, you birdbrain.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This is the heart of Sami, the First Forest.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Where we come from, and where we go.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Prepare some food as tribute to Sami, and we can enter.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Would bad things happen if we don't?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Who knows? Do you want to find out?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Er, never mind.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is hardtack okay?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Crush it and spread it on the ground.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A-Alright.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Sami) Great land, we ask your leave to pass over you.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Sami) We offer you this sacrifice, that you may watch over us, and protect us from bloodshed, from being hunted.
(Sami) Sami says it's okay, ladies.
(Sami) It will eat well thanks to your generosity.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Isn't that a little... casual? Young shaman.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...Apprentice shaman.
This isn't really a formal occasion, after all. Sami wouldn't mind the presence of a child of the Santalla Tree.
A shaman, a hunter, and an outlander? That's a rare sight.
I don't suppose you're here just for the experience?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: We're in a hurry to head south, and don't have time to go around the First Land.
I see. My teacher often takes this shortcut too.
Not this time, though. He left me here alone to 'experience the Samivilinn.'
I've been here for days, wandering the woods without a sliver of revelation to be found.
You should know what I mean, child of the tree.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Please, call me Santalla.
Very well, Santalla. Can you tell me what our teachers expect us to bring back from here?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I do not know, oak-child. I have only been here to witness. This is not where my trial was.
Is that so? What a shame.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: We have a long road ahead of us. Let's hurry.
Hmm...
Wait!
I'll come with you.
I know the trees with the best shade, the cleanest streams, and the safest animal trails.
I can be your guide!
There's no one more qualified!
Let me come with you, Santalla. I'm so bored here I could turn into a tree.
What do you think, great shaman?
And what about you, hunter? Or our outlander friend?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I guess I don't mind...
We're all agreed, then?
Let's go, then! Welcome to the First Forest!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: One more question, oak-child.
Hm? What is it?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: What should we call you?
Me? Hm...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: My Sami name might be a little hard to remember... My teacher calls me Oakcup, so you can too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: May I ask how you got that name?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Because he always grabs my horn and tries to drink from it when he's drunk.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey, are we being watched?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Like, by a deity...?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Big predators. One on the tree, one behind Simone in the bushes, and one behind that tree to the left.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, is that all?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: After all the weird stuff we've encountered, dealing with carnivorous wildlife seems almost quaint.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Should I be ready for a fight then?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No need. They're not hungry enough to risk attacking.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: So stop worrying about their dinner and start worrying about ours—!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh? Look out!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Need help?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No thanks, I'm done.
A tuskbeast lies prone on the ground, glaring at Typhon.
A gaping wound stretches from its cheek all the way to its foreleg.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I guess one of them was hungry enough. Terrible choice of prey, though.

spans.text: hungry enough. Terrible choice of prey, though.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Go. Your meat tastes terrible anyway.
The tuskbeast does not seem willing to leave. It crouches down in the shadows, ready to attack again.
Bang!
A loud bang rings out in the air before it, sending it scampering into the distance and leaving behind only a scattered trail of blood.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Did you just shoot something with your finger, Typhon?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Yeah, for scaring away big guys like these.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A roll of leaves?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You wrap up air with leaves until it forms a ball.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Takes notes)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But how do you wrap air with leaves?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Don't ask. I've tried to teach others, but no one's ever been able to learn it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Easy, it's just an unlucky hornbeast that got its neck bitten in half. Maybe by the one that attacked us, maybe by another.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Looks like our outlander friend has grown accustomed to the ways of this land.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: A few more weeks of this, and she'll be a fully-fledged Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ahaha...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: An outlander who understands Sami. How nice.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I remember working as a guide for some Columbian tourists while on a pilgrimage.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: They started screaming when they saw some carnivores doing their carnivoring. Apparently, they thought it was too bloody and uncivilized.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Not that I'd call myself civilized, but didn't they pay good money to come here and see the 'untamed wilderness'?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: One of them even tried to stop the beasts, and nearly ended up as their next meal.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Their clothes were dignified enough, but certainly not the people wearing them.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You have quite a mastery of Columbian.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Ursine) Not just Columbian! I just can't keep my mouth shut. Guess I'm a natural-born chatterbox.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: And I suppose my teacher was a weird old man for teaching me all that.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Broken Sami) Know.. a bit... ah, yes, true.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: The folks back home hate it when I just strike up a conversation with southerners. One time, there was a regular Ursus caravan that passed through the tribal market, and...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (When was the last time I returned?)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (The breath of the wild continues to echo through this place...)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Does Amma still watch over this forest?)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Something isn't right.)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (The influence of Amma lingers... but it's not alone.)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (The Black Mark of Ursus...)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What is it, Simone?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Has our guide found somewhere we can spend the night?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yup, inside that tree up ahead.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Cup says it's hollow, with enough room for the four of us.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I've never seen a hollow tree before.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Then now's your chance.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wow, we could easily fit another person or two in here!

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: It's the largest tree house around. Could hold close to a dozen.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Where's Typhon?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: The hunter? She went looking for musbeast fruit stashes. She wanted something extra for dinner.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You should rest. I'll set up some protection.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Is that really necessary? The tree's already been blessed, and there are even talismans hanging off of it.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: She's so serious.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That's how Simone is. I'd have frozen to death three, maybe four times by now if she weren't here to help.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Simone? Hm... Simone... Santalla... I think I've heard that name.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is she someone famous in Sami?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Oh... No, not at all. I must be remembering wrong.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I have a hard time keeping track of anything I haven't seen for myself on my pilgrimage.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: So maybe I'm mixing her up with someone else.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Opens notebook)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You seem to know a lot, Cup. Mind if I ask a few questions?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Shoot.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I picked up two pieces of bark from a tree. And they had symbols on them.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I want to know what they mean.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: It's a code that Sami uses to communicate with us.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: They could be messages about the past, the future, or about nature.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: The same symbols can also mean very different things, depending on who is receiving them and when.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: May I have a look?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I have them right here.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: This is... the old tree's bark...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: 'Snowpriest'... 'Delight'...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Looks like a message from a clan tree to its shaman. You can have them back.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What's the difference between a 'Snowpriest' and 'shaman'?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Think of a Snowpriest as the head shaman or a greater shaman. He may not be the oldest, but he's certainly the highest in status, the most powerful, and the local leader.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Incidentally, my teacher is a Snowpriest.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Will... you become one too?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Nah, it's such a pain taking care of the tribe and solving all their problems. Leave that to someone who wants the job.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So... are you a shaman now?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Nope, just an apprentice. I have no idea what Sami wants, or even what it wants from me.

spans.text: Nope, just an apprentice. I have no idea what Sami wants, or even what it wants from

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Which is why my teacher made me come here to feel the Samivilinn.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And have you felt it?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Leaves fall, rivers flow. It's all the same. I don't feel anything unusual.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I have plenty of complaints for him the next time I see him.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You're back, Simone!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Let me have a look.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Wow. You can really do that with ground frost?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: By the way, I heard that the one who serves the old tree can control the wind and snow, making them dance at her fingertips.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: The old tree takes no servants, nor does it need one like me.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Well, if you don't want to talk, I'm not going to press the matter.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Old tree... Is there a difference between the clan trees?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: There's only one tree that can be called old in Sami.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: It represents the Past, and often appears with the heralds of the Present and the Future.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: The three are separate but one, transcending Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The Past...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: By your outfit, I thought you were an explorer.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: You seem more like—

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: What's the word?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: A folklorist?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: As an explorer, it's always good to learn more about an unfamiliar place.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I'll bring you some Sami books if we ever meet again, explorer.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That'd be great!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: On the other hand, there's only so much I can carry in extreme environments... Maybe the equivalent of two volumes of the 'Encyclopedia Columbiana.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's about this long, this wide, and this thick... hardcover.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Yeah, not sure why you thought that'd help me at all. Just give me your luggage and let me feel the weight.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, it's all bundled up to be carried on my back. One second.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: There.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's all on the ground.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Hm. Good, looks like you can fit it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: That's about the same weight as two Sami books.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Er... what sort of books?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Legends, tribal history, that sort of thing.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: But a full tribal history takes up enough wooden tablets to fill an entire tree house, so I'll spare you that.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I-I thought the paper books I saw in the Cyclops's cave were Sami books...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maggy!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, welcome back.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you have any more of those flare sticks?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yeah, why?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I tried one when I was picking the fruits, and it worked even better than the leaf ball.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You mean you ran into a tuskbeast?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Why wouldn't I? I was walking alone in the forest and they're hungry.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Anyway, do you have any?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Half a bundle. How many do you need?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Give me two for now.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And here, fruit from a musbeast stash. I've washed them with water.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Thanks!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Let's eat together and get to bed early. I don't want to wake up and find the door blocked by a bunch of hungry beasts.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I'll take the night watch.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You already stayed up the other night. It should be my turn.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: It's safer here, and I won't be up all night. Consider it a chance for me to relax.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Alright... if you say so.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (Whisper) Be careful. There are demons in the forest.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Let's make a campfire, Simone.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Absolutely not!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you want to draw the attention of every predator in the forest?!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A-A lamp, then?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Not much difference between a lamp and a fire, light-wise.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: If you can't sleep, then try this.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: A dreamcatcher. Helps you pass the night in peace, with no dreams of becoming prey.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'll be going to bed, then.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Good night.
As Oakcup promised, Magallan was not troubled by nightmares that night.
Instead, she dreamed another dream.
In it, she is still in the forest at night.
But she is not alone.
She is a creature like Emperor.
Beside her, a massive white hornbeast slumbers in the dream of another.
It was serene and beautiful. Magallan could not help but reach out to caress It.
But It is so dignified and solemn that her hand stops in mid-air.
She decides to lay down next to It and dream together with It.
A dream within a dream.
In it, a dark shadow shambles towards the tree hole where the group is sleeping.
Behind it is a trail of darkness and filth.
Black snow falls from the sky, burning away Santalla's frost and creating a gap.
The shadow walks towards the gap, leaving its vile trail on the ground.
Suddenly, a hornbeast catches its attention.
The hornbeast leaps and disappears. By the time the shadow turns around, the gap is filled with frost again.
It gazes upon the frost, and shambles towards where the hornbeast disappeared.
The hornbeast is still by Magallan when she wakes up.
But Its horn had begun to melt.
Then Its body, then the forest.
Magallan sits upon the snow, snowflakes falling on her beak.
For some reason, she feels regret.
She never sees the hornbeast's eyes, until the dream vanishes.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're up early today.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I just happened to wake up...
Perhaps that was not the entire story. Her sleeping bag is wet near the pocket.
She remembers pulling the pocket's zipper shut before sleeping, but it is open now, as if something fell out.
There was nothing missing though—
Except a little Sami souvenir.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Typhon...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What's the matter? Got out the wrong side of bed?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Does Amma's Affection disappear?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mother has to take care of so many. She can't stay by your side forever.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Did the Affection I gave you melt?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maybe that's a good thing.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maybe she took care of a big problem for us, without us even realizing.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If possible, I'd have liked to keep it with me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Well, we can always find another. It's not that hard.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, okay!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That's... the beast that attacked us the other day.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hasn't been dead for long.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Looks like it was rammed to death by a large herbivore.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Self-defense, to avoid being eaten?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No, it came for revenge while the predator was weakened.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Maybe it lost a friend or family when it was little, and sought vengeance once it grew up.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Animals, seeking revenge...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: The hunter kills its prey, and the offspring takes revenge. Humans do that, and so do animals.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: We're not as different from them as you 'civilized' folk believe.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: But that aside... hunter, shaman, over here. We have a bigger problem.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Simone... this rockhorn...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Yes, a demon did this.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Take the foal away, oak-child. Don't let it lick the mother's blood.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Gotcha.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Imitates a rockhorn cry)
The foal hears the call and staggers away from its mother and towards Oakcup.

steps.name: Baby Rockhorn
steps.text: (Sobbing cry)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: It's scared. Don't worry, I'm here.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Licks the baby rockhorn's forehead)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Picks up her camera)
Click—
Magallan looks at the photo.
With her own eyes, she can clearly see the rockhorn bleeding blood as black as ink.
But the blood doesn't appear in the photo at all.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: It wasn't caused directly by a demon, just a corrupted creature, some kind of beast.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: It won't be turned.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Can you save it, oak-child?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: One second. Watch over the baby for a bit, Magallan.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Imitates a rockhorn cry)
Oakcup leads the foal to Magallan, then heads towards the injured rockhorn.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: H-Hello?
Magallan stretches out her hand, and the foal happily rubs its head against her palm.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Low cry)

steps.name: Rockhorn
steps.text: (Pained cry)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Not good... We might've had a chance if we'd arrived earlier, but now...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: All we can do is ease its pain.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Stand aside, hunter.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Don't let the foal see.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Long call)

steps.name: Rockhorn
steps.text: (Stifled moan)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: No need to be afraid. It won't hurt.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Waves staff)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Sleep now. Roam free in dream.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Over hills, over swamp♪

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Puts down staff and takes out dagger)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Rest in Amma's woods, for she watches over you♪

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: No more pain, no more suffering♪

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: With the souls of all life—

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Pierces the rockhorn's throat with the dagger)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Roam free on Sami's back♪

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Rest now, soul of the land...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Oo... (imitates rockhorn mother's cry)

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh...
Hearing the call, the foal hurries to Oakcup's side.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Low cry)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (High-pitched call)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Fear not. Your mother is with you.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: With her blood... her tears...

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Draws the bloodied dagger across the mother rockhorn's eye)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Her horn.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Criss-crosses with the dagger)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Stopping at your...?
The foal lightly kicks Oakcup's knee with its hoof.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Hoof.)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Draws a mark on the hoof with the dagger)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Go, friend. Your life has just begun.
The foal continues to circle Oakcup, seemingly seeing him as its new family.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Well... I suppose that works.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Only until we take care of your mother, though.
The foal does not answer, only rubbing itself against Oakcup.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: What's the plan?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: This is more than an apprentice can handle.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: (Sharp whistle)

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Screw training. I'll let my teacher take care of it.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: That way will take you out of the forest towards a nearby marshfolk village. They'll give you a warm welcome.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I'll stay here with the kid and stop the rockhorn's bleeding until my teacher arrives. I can't let it become food for scavengers.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Say hello to the Canopy Sage for me.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Oh, so you knew—

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Tell him that this is connected to the Black Mark of Ursus.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Black Mark of Ursus? Alright, I'll pass it on.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Nothing good ever comes of Ursus being involved.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you have enough rations?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I'm not about to become the first apprentice shaman to starve to death in the forest.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Here, take this.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: A flashlight?

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: I can see well enough in the dark, but it might be useful to the old man. Thanks.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: Farewell, friends.

steps.name: Oakcup
steps.text: May Sami keep you safe.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Finally, out of the woods!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey, I think I'm getting a signal.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The marshfolk trade with you guys a lot, so they've got some of your metal things set up.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What will Cup do with the rockhorn's carcass?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Cleanse the corrupted soil and blood, clean the wound, then leave it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Shouldn't it be buried?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No point. Scavengers would just dig it out.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is it the same with people?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: More or less.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Like Oakcup said, here in Sami there's not much difference between humans and beasts.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hunt and be hunted. Eat and be eaten.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The best we can do is show our prey a bit of kindness and make sure they're dead before we eat them.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: That's the law of nature, the will of the north, the Samivilinn.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: If you want to change that, there's only one way.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What's that?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Become Sami itself. Become the All-Father.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Of course, that's just a legend. No one's ever seen it happen, haha.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Stop messing with me...
'Checking status of Black Mark. Liebafowl is about to trade with those upon water.'
Another carcass, another victim.
The hunter steps over the hunted, with no intention to feed.
This was not to satiate hunger, nor for revenge, but pure and simple killing.
It is a hornbeast, a corrupted one, with an empty hole on its abdomen, but it is still 'alive.'
Its blood, tears, and saliva are all black as ink.
The hunter roams the animal trail, looking for a new victim.
There is a figure swaying at the same frequency, not far away.
It is clearly human.
Its unique and rhythmic breathing can be heard clearly, even without approaching.
Hiss... huff...
